_meta: FIELD REPORT (the gap): a project's gates encoded environment PREMISES (dev-mode, specific data volumes, no-real-calls). Mid-project the premises died (volumes deleted, real calls needed while still in active dev). The gates then failed as gate_blocked, every agent correctly recited 'never weaken the gate', and the human had to hand-edit the gates to carry on — the revision happened anyway, but OUTSIDE the system: no review, no re-audit, no recorded reason. The 'never weaken' rule protected the letter of rigor and lost the substance. The system already half-admits gates rot (gate_rot recovery text says 're-point the gate') but only for completed phases + deleted files, and offers no sanctioned path. DESIGN: `hb regate` — gate revision as a first-class, audited operation. Not a weakening mechanism: a RE-GROUNDING mechanism whose invariant is 'a gate changes only through the same rigor that created it' — including that acceptance after a revision requires a FRESH pass of the revised criteria. DECLARE: `hb regate <GATE|PHASE> <reason>` (node: trailing words; python: --reason — the park arg-style precedent, divergence documented in parity-notes) requires a non-empty reason AND a set HB_ACTOR (the constraints --record precedent, fail-closed on identity), snapshots the gate's current criteria into gates[G].regate = {at, reason, actor, prev_criteria, pending:true} (the diff stays inspectable), appends an audit-only gate_regated event, and refuses a second declare while one is pending. The author then edits the criteria in dag.json — the plan is editable; regate is what makes the edit LOUD, attributed and gated. PERIMETER while pending (fail-closed, RG1) — the refusal sites are the CHOKEPOINTS, not the CLI wrappers: node gate.sh refuses in eval (single, --check, and --all — where a pending-regate gate is COUNTED FAILING regardless of ever-passed/planned status: a sweep must never say ALL GREEN over an unrefuted revision) with a DISTINCT EXIT CODE 3 (1 = blocked, 2 = usage — the refusal is machine-distinguishable); python refuses in gate.py eval_gate itself (so run/check/all AND hb diagnose can never execute a pending gate's criteria — the premises died, execution itself can do harm), in review_policy.accept_review for ALL THREE verdicts (the one place the review rules live — the CLI, the MCP review tool and any API caller all route through it), and in constraints.record; node hb.js review (pass|fail|free) and constraints --record refuse likewise. Every refusal: loud line naming the regate + reason, NO gate_passed/gate_failed/review_* event appended. UNATTENDED SURFACES (RG1): the executors escalate and STOP on the refusal signal (gate.sh exit 3 / python run_gate regate_pending status) — never auto-rearm, never busy-loop; the python executor's refuse() path must NOT append review_failed via direct mutate while a regate is pending (it escalates instead), and node hb-exec wraps its review-fail call so a CLI refusal escalates rather than crashing; the tick (both runtimes) sleeps out a non-wake `regate_pending_waiting` reason when the pending gate carries a pending regate (the gate_blocked_waiting_human precedent: sleep_out reasons are not PROTOCOL keys, so the no-new-PROTOCOL-keys non-goal survives; identical reason string both runtimes, parity-cased). REARM (RG2): `hb regate <G> --rearm --artifact <file> [--model <m>]` refused unless ALL hold: a pending regate exists; HB_ACTOR is set and differs from the declaring actor (case-insensitive norm — the review-pass different-actor precedent); the artifact is readable, >=40 trimmed chars, and cites a real anchor of the phase (gate id, phase id, a task id, or a path the REVISED criteria reference — the review-pass substance precedent); the full-dag deterministic audit (in-process audit()) reports 0 errors — a hollow revision cannot rearm. On success: the artifact bytes are stored at .hb/reviews/<G>.regate.md, sha256 recorded on an audit-only gate_rearmed event and a rearm record on the dag ({at, actor, model, artifact, sha256}), pending clears, evaluation re-enables. STALE-PASS INVALIDATION (RG2): a pre-regate deterministic pass must not launder through — a review verdict is REFUSED while the gate's last gate_passed predates its last gate_rearmed (pure event-order check, the reviewCycle technique, no projection change): acceptance requires a fresh pass of the revised criteria — and the fresh pass must be PROVENANCED: only a gate_passed carrying the evidence fields a real evaluation records (non-empty criteria / runtime — gate.sh and gate.py both stamp them) counts as newer-than-rearm; a bare synthetic pass (hb import writes {event:gate_passed, gate} with no provenance) can NEVER satisfy the check or clear doctor's stale-accepted problem; doctor flags as a PROBLEM an ACCEPTED gate whose last gate_rearmed is newer than its last provenanced gate_passed (evidence is stale — re-run the gate). CONSTRAINT-SET BOUNDARY (RG2): gate-time constraints — and every other per-cycle artifact — are authored against what the phase changed under the OLD criteria, so nothing recorded before the declare may survive into the post-rearm acceptance. The boundary is defined ONCE per runtime as the CYCLE START: node reviewCycle.start and python's single shared cycle-start computation (constraints.py review_cycle AND review_cycle_full must derive it from one place — today review_cycle_full recomputes start independently, a latent divergence this wave removes) become the LATER of the gate's last review verdict and its last gate_rearmed. Everything that keys on the cycle moves together: 'recorded' (a fresh gate-time set is owed and recordable after a rearm — write-once afresh), AND the profile free_review-in-this-cycle check (review_policy and hb.js review pass both consume start): a free review recorded before the declare does not satisfy the post-rearm acceptance — a fresh free review is owed too. Shared logic, parity-cased. PARK COMPOSITION (RG1): park retires, regate refuses — they compose with no special casing except visibility: declaring on a parked gate and parking during a pending regate are both allowed (eval/acceptance stay refused regardless, so nothing launders); the --all sweep's parked listing ANNOTATES a parked gate whose regate is pending (parked AND regate pending) so retirement never hides an unrefuted revision, while parked gates still do not fail the sweep (park's retirement contract). DOCTOR (RG2): a pending regate is a NOTE (legitimate in-flight state); a missing/thin/byte-changed rearm artifact is a PROBLEM (the free-review re-check precedent); MARKER CROSS-CHECK: the event log is truth — when the last gate_regated for a gate has no later gate_rearmed yet dag.json carries no pending marker (e.g. dag.json restored from backup per the dag_corrupted recovery), doctor raises a PROBLEM naming the divergence. DIAGNOSE (RG2): a structured regate branch — names the gate, the recorded reason, and the exact recovery commands — reachable explicitly (hb diagnose regate_pending) and by inference; PRECEDENCE: when the gate a diagnose branch is about to blame carries a pending regate, that branch routes to the rearm recovery (gate_blocked/review_stuck must not print commands the perimeter then refuses), and bare inference prefers the regate branch when the blocking gate is the regated one. SURFACING (RG3): hb report marks a pending-regate gate loudly on both runtimes; dev docs current-state — including the TRUST-MODEL HONESTY line: the rearm bar is procedural evidence within the existing self-declared HB_ACTOR trust model, not mechanical proof; the human reviews the prev_criteria diff (dev docs must say so, never sell the bar as proof), and the pytest-via-.venv precondition (system python3 has no pytest on this machine; gate criteria pin py/.venv/bin/python). DELIBERATE NON-GOALS this wave (deferred, not forgotten): no new tick PROTOCOL reason keys (regate_pending_waiting is a sleep_out reason, not a wake); no MCP regate tool (the park precedent — and the MCP review tool is covered because it routes through accept_review); no change to the shared audit RULESET (surfacing is runtime+doctor+report; an audit finding would touch the parity-pinned verbatim ruleset — next wave if wanted); no criteria-hash tamper detection for UNSANCTIONED hand-edits beyond the doctor marker cross-check (regate offers the sanctioned path; full tamper detection is its own feature); the `detach` verb and the discovery how-to/doctrine text are the NEXT wave. DOCTRINE BOUNDARY (for the wave-2 how-to, stated here for the refuter): regate re-grounds a gate whose premises died; it must never be the escape hatch from a failing bar — the rearm evidence bar + stale-pass invalidation are the mechanical enforcement, and the loud prev_criteria diff is what a human reviews. REFUTATION ROUND 1 (strong model): UNSOUND — 2 BLOCKING (non-CLI acceptance paths: accept_review/MCP/executor bypass + executor crash; refusal-with-no-event livelocked unattended runs), 3 MAJOR (stale-pass laundering; python eval_gate/diagnose leak; never-passed sweep ALL-GREEN), 4 MINOR (marker cross-check; trust-model honesty; venv pytest + node-suite 12min measured timing; diagnose precedence). ALL folded above. REFUTATION ROUND 2 (strong model, fresh): UNSOUND — 1 BLOCKING (the python executor has a SECOND direct review_failed writer on its unconstrained refuted-branch besides refuse(), and the review-owed unattended fixture was missing, so the node crash-wrap had no reachable teeth), 3 MAJOR (a pre-declare gate-time constraint set survived into the post-rearm acceptance with no sanctioned re-record — the reviewCycle boundary decision above; hb import's synthetic gate_passed could fabricate the fresh pass — the provenance decision above; the lint shape-validation had no deterministic teeth: two lints silently accepting a malformed record were 'identical' and green), 2 MINOR (park composition undefined — decided above; no parity floor pinning the new cases' existence + GATE_RG3 ran no parity although rg3b edits both runtimes). ALL folded: the executor invariant is now ANY-path ('the executor never appends review_failed while the gate's regate is pending'), the unattended proof gains the det-passed/review-owed fixture driven through both executors on refuted:true AND refuted:false, both ticks sleep regate_pending_waiting from the review_pending state too, the proofs assert lint errors non-empty on malformed records, parity criteria carry grep floors for the regate cases, and GATE_RG3 gained a parity criterion. REFUTATION ROUND 3 (strong model, fresh): UNSOUND — 1 BLOCKING (the round-2 tick-sleep fold intercepted both unattended fixtures before the executor guards could run: executors exit IDLE on a non-wake tick, so the any-path invariant was vacuously green and its selftest teeth unsatisfiable — folded: the three-fixture reachability scheme above, with the mid-review race, the one-shot gate-path tick shim, and pinned selftest guard-strips), 1 MAJOR (the cycle boundary moved only 'recorded' while the free-review check consumes the cycle start too, and python computed start in two independent places — folded: the single CYCLE-START definition above), 1 MINOR (wording dropped 'provenanced' — fixed). REFUTATION ROUND 4 (strong model, fresh): SOUND — the ordering analysis found no acceptance that evades the perimeter + stale-pass + cycle-start trio; 1 MAJOR residual folded (the post-rearm resumption window: a resumed executor on review_pending with a stale pass must escalate without dispatching or writing any review event — the invariant window is 'pending OR stale', node's wrap generalized to ANY CLI refusal), 2 MINOR residuals folded (rg2p floors on 'rearm'; two residual unprovenanced wordings).

GATE_RG1.desc: regate declare works on both runtimes and the fail-closed perimeter is complete at the CHOKEPOINTS: while a regate is pending, no path evaluates or accepts the gate — gate.sh single/--check/--all (exit 3; sweep counts it failing in both ever-passed and never-passed states), python eval_gate (so diagnose can't execute criteria), review_policy.accept_review (all verdicts — CLI, MCP and API callers), constraints recording, node review/constraints verbs — all refuse loudly, append no gate/review event; executors escalate and stop (bounded, no crash, no fabricated review_failed); ticks sleep out regate_pending_waiting; lint validates the record shape identically; parity-cased.

review.prompt: Refute that RG1 is done. Was tests/regate-fail-closed.sh actually RED before rg1b/rg1c/rg1f (spec-first — check the log/diff order), and does --selftest prove each assertion load-bearing (strip a guard from a copy → the matching check must go red)? Is the perimeter COMPLETE at the chokepoints — try to find a path that still evaluates or accepts a pending-regate gate: gate.sh single/--check/--all; python eval_gate driven through hb gate AND through hb diagnose (plant a side-effecting criterion — does diagnose execute it?); review_policy.accept_review driven DIRECTLY via python -c for pass, fail AND free (not just the CLI); node hb review all three verdicts; constraints recording on both runtimes. Is gate.sh's refusal really exit 3 (distinct from 1 and 2), and does the --all sweep COUNT a pending-regate gate as failing when the gate has passed before AND when it never passed (the planned-skip hole) — or can it still print ALL GREEN? Does any refusal path append a gate_passed/gate_failed/review_* event (run it and read events.jsonl — it must not)? UNATTENDED — check REACHABILITY first (a pre-declared regate makes the ticks sleep and the executors exit idle, so those fixtures cannot exercise the executor guards; the plan's race and shim fixtures exist precisely for that): does the MID-REVIEW RACE fixture (the backend itself declares the regate before returning its verdict) actually reach both executors' review paths on refuted:true AND refuted:false — events.jsonl free of EVERY review_* event, including the python executor's unconstrained refuted-branch direct st.mutate (not just refuse()), node's wrapped review-fail call escalating instead of throwing? Does the GATE-PATH shim fixture deliver exit 3 / regate_pending to each executor's escalation branch? Does --selftest strip the two python writer guards AND the node wrap, each flipping a named check red — or would a weakened guard survive the selftest? Do both ticks return wakeAgent:false with the IDENTICAL regate_pending_waiting string from BOTH states, with the executors exiting bounded/idle there? LINT TEETH: does a malformed regate record produce a NON-EMPTY error on each lint (not merely identical-possibly-empty verdicts)? PARK: does the --all parked listing annotate a parked gate's pending regate while parked gates still don't fail the sweep? Does declare resolve BOTH a phase id and a gate id, refuse a second declare while pending, refuse an empty reason and an unset HB_ACTOR, and snapshot prev_criteria byte-faithfully? Is the lint shape-validation real on BOTH lints (feed a malformed record to each)? Is the parity case wired so a divergence — including the sleep-reason string — would actually fail it? End SOUND or UNSOUND.

constraints.claim: While gates[G].regate.pending is true, every evaluation and acceptance path refuses fail-closed at the chokepoints on both runtimes: gate.sh single/--check refuse with exit 3 and the --all sweep counts the gate failing in BOTH ever-passed and never-passed fixture states; python's refusal lives in gate.py eval_gate (hb diagnose cannot execute a pending gate's criteria) and review_policy.accept_review refuses all three verdicts for every caller (CLI, MCP review tool, direct API); node review/constraints verbs and python constraints.record refuse; no refusal appends a gate_passed/gate_failed/review_* event.
constraints.violation: Any invocation — gate.sh <G>/--check/--all (either fixture state), python hb gate (any form), hb diagnose, accept_review driven directly or via the MCP review tool, hb review pass|fail|free, constraints recording — evaluates criteria, exits 0, appends a gate/review event, uses exit 1/2 instead of the distinct refusal signal, or the sweep reports ALL GREEN over a pending regate.

constraints.claim: Declare is attributed and snapshotted: it requires a non-empty reason and a set HB_ACTOR, records {reason, actor, prev_criteria, pending:true} with prev_criteria an exact copy of the criteria at declare time, appends an audit-only gate_regated event that leaves the state projection unchanged, resolves both a phase id and a gate id, and refuses a second declare while one is pending.
constraints.violation: A declare succeeds with no reason or with HB_ACTOR unset/unknown; prev_criteria differs from the pre-declare criteria; state.json changes from the event; or a second declare overwrites the pending snapshot.

constraints.claim: Unattended surfaces never busy-loop, crash or bypass, with every guard REACHABLE in a proof fixture: both ticks sleep out the identical non-PROTOCOL reason regate_pending_waiting from the gate_pending AND the review_pending state (executors exiting bounded/idle); the mid-review race (the backend declares the regate before returning its verdict) exercises the ANY-path executor invariant on refuted:true and refuted:false — no review_* event while pending, covering refuse(), the unconstrained refuted-branch st.mutate, the accept path, and node hb-exec's wrapped review-fail call; the gate-path signal (one-shot tick shim) delivers gate.sh exit 3 / run_gate regate_pending to each executor's escalation branch; the selftest strips each executor guard and the wrap, flipping named checks red.
constraints.violation: hb-exec.js run or hb exec run loops without bound or crashes unhandled on either fixture, any review_* event lands in events.jsonl while pending (through refuse(), the unconstrained refuted-branch, or an accept), the two ticks emit different sleep reasons, or a tick wakes gate_pending or review_pending unconditionally over a pending regate.

constraints.claim: The regate record is lint-validated with teeth and identical results on both runtimes — a malformed record produces a NON-EMPTY error on each lint (asserted deterministically, not only compared), a well-formed record lints clean — and the parity case pins declare + perimeter cross-runtime (a declare written by one runtime is honored — marker read, evaluation refused with the equivalent signal — by the other).
constraints.violation: A malformed regate record lints clean on both runtimes, or passes one lint and fails the other, or a fixture declared via node evaluates under python (or vice versa), or the parity case would stay green through such a divergence.

criteria.desc: the fail-closed proof passes (declare + full perimeter + unattended surfaces, both runtimes)
teeth: each perimeter assertion individually load-bearing (--selftest)
python declare+perimeter+unattended cases green (py/.venv pytest — system python3 has none)
full parity green including the new regate case(s) — with a floor pinning the cases exist

GATE_RG2.desc: rearm enforces the full evidence bar (pending exists; different actor; substantive artifact citing the phase; audit-clean dag), stores the artifact with sha256 provenance, re-enables evaluation, invalidates stale pre-regate passes (review verdicts refused until a fresh pass of the revised criteria), and doctor/diagnose surface pending, altered-evidence, stale-accepted and marker-divergence states with regate-aware precedence — both runtimes, parity-cased.

review.prompt: Refute that RG2 is done. Try to rearm around the bar on BOTH runtimes: no pending regate; HB_ACTOR unset; the SAME actor who declared but with different letter case; a 39-trimmed-char artifact; an artifact citing nothing from the phase; a revised gate left hollow (audit error) — any acceptance refutes. STALE-PASS LAUNDERING: build the sharp fixture — det pass recorded, review owed, declare, edit criteria, valid rearm — then attempt hb review pass (and fail, and free) on node AND via python accept_review directly: any verdict accepted before a FRESH gate_passed lands after the gate_rearmed refutes; after a fresh pass, the review must proceed. Then attack the fresh-pass rule itself: run `hb import` after the rearm — does its synthetic bare gate_passed unlock the verdicts or clear doctor's stale-accepted problem (it must not: only a provenanced pass counts)? CONSTRAINT SURVIVAL: record a gate-time set BEFORE the declare, then rearm and fresh-pass — is the old set still consulted (it must not be: the cycle START is the later of verdict and rearm), can a fresh set be recorded (it must be), and do BOTH runtimes' review cycles agree (shared logic — check the parity case covers it)? FREE-REVIEW SURVIVAL: on a free_review-profile gate, record the free review BEFORE the declare, then rearm and fresh-pass — does review pass accept on the stale free review (it must not: the free-review check consumes the same moved cycle start — verify python's review_cycle_full derives start from the SAME computation as review_cycle, not its own)? After a VALID rearm: does evaluation truly run again; are the stored bytes at .hb/reviews/<G>.regate.md exactly what sha256 on gate_rearmed pins; and does doctor actually flag deletion, emptying, AND a one-byte change of that file? Does doctor flag an ACCEPTED gate whose last gate_rearmed is newer than its last PROVENANCED gate_passed, and the marker-divergence fixture (gate_regated in the log, no later gate_rearmed, no dag marker — simulated backup restore)? Is the pending-regate doctor NOTE present? Does bare `hb diagnose` INFER regate_pending when it is the only blocker, and do the gate_blocked/review_stuck branches route to the rearm recovery when their gate carries a pending regate (plant a stale gate_failed and a pending review and check the printed commands are not ones the perimeter refuses)? Was tests/regate-rearm.sh RED first, and does --selftest give each refusal row teeth? Do the parity cases actually compare both runtimes on the same fixture bytes, including the stale-pass refusal and the doctor lines? End SOUND or UNSOUND.

constraints.claim: Every row of the rearm refusal matrix refuses loudly on both runtimes and leaves pending untouched: no pending regate; HB_ACTOR unset; actor equal to the declaring actor under case-insensitive comparison; artifact missing, under 40 trimmed chars, or citing no real phase anchor; dag not audit-clean (in-process deterministic audit reports any error).
constraints.violation: Any matrix row clears pending, writes a rearm record, appends gate_rearmed, or stores an artifact.

constraints.claim: A successful rearm is fully provenanced, re-enabling, and non-laundering: artifact bytes stored at .hb/reviews/<G>.regate.md with sha256 + actor + model on the audit-only gate_rearmed event and the dag rearm record, state projection unchanged, both runtimes' gate evaluation subsequently runs criteria normally — every review verdict is refused (node review verb and python accept_review alike) while the gate's last PROVENANCED gate_passed predates its last gate_rearmed, until a fresh pass of the revised criteria lands, and a resumed executor in that stale window escalates without dispatching a backend or writing any review event on either runtime.
constraints.violation: Evaluation stays refused after a valid rearm; the stored artifact or its sha256 pin is absent; a review verdict is accepted over a deterministic pass that predates the rearm (the stale pre-regate pass launders into an acceptance, tag and anchor); a synthetic import-written gate_passed satisfies the fresh-pass rule; or a gate-time constraint set recorded before the declare is still consulted after the rearm (the review accepted against pre-revision targets, or no fresh set is recordable).

constraints.claim: Doctor and diagnose surface every regate state with regate-aware precedence: pending → note; rearm artifact missing/thin/byte-changed → problem; accepted gate with gate_rearmed newer than its last PROVENANCED gate_passed → problem (a bare synthetic pass never clears it); event log attesting an unanswered gate_regated while dag.json lacks the marker → problem; diagnose names gate, reason and runnable recovery explicitly AND by inference, and the gate_blocked/review_stuck branches route to the rearm recovery instead of printing commands the perimeter refuses.
constraints.violation: Doctor stays silent on a deleted/emptied/altered rearm artifact, a stale-accepted gate, or the marker-divergence fixture; or diagnose cannot surface a pending regate without being handed the reason; or a diagnose branch tells the agent to run a command the perimeter then refuses.

constraints.claim: Parity: the acceptance, every refusal row, the stale-pass review refusal, and the cycle-start rearm boundary (recorded = false after a rearm even when a pre-declare set exists; a pre-declare free review not satisfying the post-rearm cycle) behave identically across runtimes on the same fixture bytes, and the doctor note/problem lines carry the same substance.
constraints.violation: A rearm (or refusal, or stale-pass verdict refusal) accepted by one runtime is decided differently by the other, the two runtimes disagree on whether a cycle has a recorded constraint set — or a satisfying free review — after a rearm, or doctor's regate lines diverge in substance between runtimes.

criteria.desc: the rearm proof passes (refusal matrix + success + stale-pass invalidation + doctor + diagnose, both runtimes)
teeth: each refusal row individually load-bearing (--selftest)
full parity green including the rearm case(s) — with a floor pinning the rearm surface is cased

Render reports on a pending-regate fixture with BOTH runtimes — is the marker loud (gate id + revised + rearm pending + reason), is it GONE after a valid rearm, and is a never-regated project's report byte-unchanged by this feature? Do the FULL node suite and full pytest pass — not just the regate groups? End SOUND or UNSOUND.

constraints.claim: Surfacing is loud, correct and non-invasive: both runtimes' reports mark a pending-regate gate with the gate id, a revision marker and the reason; the marker disappears after a valid rearm; a never-regated project's report output is byte-unchanged.
constraints.violation: A pending-regate fixture renders a report with no revision marker on either runtime, the marker survives a valid rearm, or a project with no regate renders differently than before the feature.

constraints.claim: Docs are current-state and honest: every regate command, flag, exit code, path and refusal documented in dev-plugin.md/dev-python.md/dev-tests.md exists verbatim in the shipped code; the new test groups, proof scripts and the py/.venv pytest precondition are listed; parity-notes records the arg-style divergence and the refusal-signal equivalence; and the trust-model honesty line is present — the rearm bar is procedural evidence within the self-declared HB_ACTOR trust model, the human reviews the prev_criteria diff.
constraints.violation: A documented command fails when run verbatim, a documented path/exit-code/message does not exist, a shipped regate behavior is absent from the dev docs, or the docs sell the rearm bar as mechanical proof.
